fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure; Walkway; Perimeter Fencing; Street Frontage; Access Drive
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Multiple Structures
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance, visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Trim or thin dense vegetation along the access drive to keep it passable for emergency vehicles.
• Clear vegetation from the sides of the access drive to maintain full vehicle-width clearance.
• Cut back vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure to create a clear gap between plants and exterior walls.
• Keep perimeter fencing gates unlocked or equipped with a breakaway latch to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.
• Mark the rear gate or fence opening nearest the detached structure so responders can locate it quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Maintain the walkway between structures free of overgrowth so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Identify a staging area on the open lawn where emergency vehicles can park without blocking the access drive.
• Post the property address visibly at the street and again at any secondary gate or fence entry point.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Open Green Space; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Route; Brush Area; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or touch the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the dense tree clusters near the structure to open up space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs and brush growing directly against the foundation and exterior walls.
• Clear low-hanging branches from large trees near the structure up to a height that separates them from ground-level plants below.
• Cut back or remove brush in the brush area closest to the structure.
• Mow or cut down tall ground vegetation surrounding the structure before dry season.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their canopies do not touch or overlap each other.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, encroaching shrubs, and tall grass along both sides.
• Maintain enough width along the driveway for emergency vehicles to pass through without obstruction.
• Remove dead branches, fallen wood, and dry plant debris from the ground around the structure.
• Create visible open ground between the base of trees and shrubs closest to the structure.
• Keep the open green space near the structure mowed short and free of dry or dead plant material.
